summary: 80-foot fire tower the DNR says was relocated to the MacKenzie Center from the State Fairgrounds; the FFLA lists it as a replica.

access.note: Grounds and trails open dawn to dusk year-round, with no vehicle sticker needed. The 40-foot platform is the highest point open to the public.

visit.trail_note: Observation platform 40 feet (12 m) above ground; the DNR asks visitors to take care climbing.

events.note: DNR says the 80-foot tower was relocated to the MacKenzie Center from the Wisconsin State Fairgrounds in West Allis. The DNR gives no date.

evidence.supports: 80-foot tower relocated to MacKenzie from the State Fairgrounds in West Allis
evidence.quote: MacKenzie's 80-foot-tall fire tower has been relocated to MacKenzie from the Wisconsin State Fairgrounds in West Allis.

evidence.supports: observation platform at 40 feet is the highest point open to the public
evidence.quote: The observation platform at 40 feet above the ground (the highest point accessible to the public)

evidence.supports: tower not in active use; gives visitors a feel for fire detection dating to 1905
evidence.quote: This tower is not in active use, but gives visitors a feel for a method of fire detection that dates back to the beginning of the U.S. Forest Service in 1905.

evidence.supports: DNR asks visitors to use caution climbing
evidence.quote: Please remember to use caution while climbing the tower.

evidence.supports: 285-acre property near Poynette in Columbia County
evidence.quote: Located on a 285-acre property near Poynette in Columbia County
The MacKenzie Center, just 25 miles north of Madison

evidence.supports: grounds and trails open dawn to dusk year-round
evidence.quote: The grounds and trails are open dawn to dusk year-round.
A vehicle admission sticker is not required at the MacKenzie Center.

evidence.supports: listed under relocated and replica lookouts
FFLA lists it as a replica from the State Fair, standing
evidence.quote: (Replica – from State Fair) Columbia 43.40082 -89.36251 Tower Standing

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on identity: the FFLA list says replica from the State Fair; the DNR calls it an 80-foot fire tower relocated from the fairgrounds and does not use the word replica. Record status 'replica' is left unchanged for a human check. No source found gives the move date, the builder or the construction date. The DNR page says the tower is not in active use, so no staffing fact is recorded.
